experiment: ie1 temporal fam codes — Reichardt correlators on the glyph lattice (the lobula-plate build)

gate.metric: primary reader: mean R2 over direction targets (sin theta, cos theta)

question: can a text-only ridge reader recover the true drift velocity of a scene from the Reichardt motion-code stream (4 pooled fam codes/frame) alone?
scene: dark field + static radial key light + static 8x8 checker (distractors) + 2 bright gaussian blobs (sigma 14-22 px, I 0.65-1.0) drifting with a GLOBAL velocity, periodic wrap

data.velocities: 8 directions x 3 speeds (0.10/0.25/0.45 frame-widths/s) x 2 reps
data.split: scene-level 34/14, seed 42 (no frame leakage: all frames of a scene stay on one side)
data.note: frames within a scene share the target; the reader generalizes across scenes

correlator.formula: Cx = S(x,y,t)*S(x-1,y,t-1) - S(x,y,t)*S(x+1,y,t-1); Cy likewise; pool = half-wave-rectified lattice sums -> mx+, mx-, my+, my-
correlator.signal_S: V=32 glyph code field (tone 0..10, edge 11+; t1 codes_for_temp convention)

readers.primary: ridge on the 4 pooled motion codes per frame (the pre-registered motion-code stream)
readers.diagnostic: ridge on the full per-cell rectified motion field (4 x rows x cols)
readers.reference: ridge on the same 4-code pooling applied to the pre-glyph lum field
readers.hygiene: t1 ridge (drop near-dead cols, center, global scale, lam=10)

settings_note: glyph dials = t1 primary pin (classic ramp, tone 100, edge 60, thresh 4, gain 10, relief 70)
measured: direction = drift angle theta = atan2(vy, vx) of the render, encoded (sin, cos); velocity = (vx, vy) in px/s; BOTH are per-scene constants recovered frame-by-frame by the readers; R2 computed on held-out scenes only
